Darjeeling tea.d: Kurseong estate planted in 1885, now Goodricke-owned, known for a rose-like fragrance and muscatel flavour.
Darjeeling tea.dt: altitude: about 980-2,300 m · teas: black, green, white, Muscatel, Moonlight

Assam & Indian black tea.d: Daga-family estate in Moran making both CTC and orthodox tea, known for golden-tipped orthodox leaf.
Sivasagar estate of 118 ha whose smoother orthodox tea is popular in Germany.
Specialty tea of the Manohari estate in Dibrugarh, described as the most expensive specialty tea.

Ceylon tea.d: High-grown western district (about 1,250-1,700 m); fresh, mild, golden-orange cup and one of the most approachable Ceylon styles.
Eastern-slope district exposed to both monsoons, with a high concentration of aromatic compounds; Thomas Lipton built part of his name on it.
Mid-grown, robust and full with a copper infusion; James Taylor planted the first commercial tea here in 1867 at Loolecondera.
Smallest of the seven districts, between Uva and Nuwara Eliya in style, with two quality seasons.
Largest district by area, mainly low-grown, with a dark golden-brown, lightly caramel cup.
Southern coastal lowlands; dark, full tea with cacao or wood notes, often used in blends.

Makaibari.d: Sold at $1,850 per kg, most expensive Indian tea
